class_name: 授受-他の授与-テクレル類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1: author → mechanical attachment gate → cold review → fixes applied → gate re-run

patterns.usage_note: The giver is the subject and the speaker or the speaker's in-group is the beneficiary, so it reports a favor done for "us" whether or not anyone asked for it; てもらう (1291) describes the very same event from the receiver's side. After an ん-euphonic te-form it surfaces as でくれる (運んでくれる). The heavily contracted ちゃくれ・じゃくれ are casual reductions of 〜てはくれ・〜ではくれ, and because that は is contrastive they occur almost only in negatives that voice a grievance: 誰も助けちゃくれない. Bare てくれ is a blunt, largely masculine command; the honorific counterpart is てくださる (1281).

examples.ruby: 友達[ともだち]が引[ひ]っ越[こ]しを手伝[てつだ]ってくれた。
examples.english: A friend pitched in and helped me move.

examples.ruby: 知[し]らない人[ひと]がバス停[てい]まで傘[かさ]に入[い]れてくれた。
examples.english: A stranger shared their umbrella with me all the way to the bus stop.

examples.ruby: 妹[いもうと]が駅[えき]まで迎[むか]えに来[き]てくれました。
examples.english: My sister was kind enough to come meet me at the station.

patterns.usage_note: The honorific (尊敬語) counterpart of てくれる: the favor-doer is someone you are elevating, such as a teacher, a client or a senior colleague. The everyday request 〜てください is the irregular imperative of this same くださる; its polite finite forms give the softer 〜てくださいませんか / 〜てくださいますか. Choose ていただく (1301) instead when you want yourself, the receiver, in the subject position.

examples.ruby: 先生[せんせい]が推薦状[すいせんじょう]を書[か]いてくださいました。
examples.english: My professor was good enough to write me a recommendation letter.

examples.ruby: 駅員[えきいん]さんが乗[の]り換[か]えの道順[みちじゅん]を丁寧[ていねい]に教[おし]えてくださった。
examples.english: The station attendant was good enough to walk me through the transfer route.

examples.ruby: 大家[おおや]さんがいつも植木[うえき]に水[みず]をやってくださいます。
examples.english: Our landlady is always good enough to water the plants for us.
